description:
CONTEXT — PREREQUISITE: flm-40e.4 (Item 2) must be complete.
After Item 2, render_vnode/2 correctly collects child fibers into the render context's new_fibers map. The reconciler must use that map as the authoritative child set instead of the stub comment.

FILE TO MODIFY: lib/filament/reconciler.ex

CURRENT STATE — reconcile_children/4 (read file for exact code):
The function has a comment: "For now, we rely on components registering themselves during render — In a full implementation, we'd parse the rendered output to find child components". The stub does partial work but does not run cleanup on unmounted fibers.

WHAT reconcile_children/4 RECEIVES
  tree: the current fiber tree (map of fiber_id => Fiber)
  parent_id: the fiber_id of the component that just re-rendered
  parent_fiber: the updated Fiber struct for parent_id
  new_fibers: map of {child_id => Fiber} collected during the render walk (from render_vnode :component and :keyed_list arms via Item 2)

TARGET BEHAVIOR

1. Compute old_child_ids: parent_fiber.children || [] (the child list from the previous render)
2. Compute new_child_ids: Map.keys(new_fibers)
3. For each child_id in old_child_ids that is NOT in new_child_ids (removed children):
   a. Fetch the fiber from tree
   b. Run cleanup for each hook slot in fiber.hook_slots:
      - {_index, {_deps, cleanup}} when is_function(cleanup, 0) -> cleanup.()
      - {_index, {:subscribed, server, _value}} -> Filament.Observable.unsubscribe(server, {owner_pid, fiber.id, index})
      - {_index, {:held, server, _token}} -> Filament.Hold.release(server, owner_pid)
      - _ -> :ok
   c. Remove the fiber from the tree (or mark :unmounting and remove — removing is cleaner)
4. Merge new_fibers into the tree (new_fibers already have status :stable from render walk)
5. Update the parent fiber's :children list to new_child_ids
6. Return the updated tree

The owner_pid for cleanup comes from opts. Read the update/4 function signature — it accepts opts keyword list with :owner_pid. Pass owner_pid through to reconcile_children.

RECURSIVE DESCENDANT CLEANUP
When removing a fiber that had its own children, those grandchildren must also be cleaned up. Implement a recursive helper:

  defp unmount_fiber(tree, fiber_id, owner_pid) do
    case Map.get(tree, fiber_id) do
      nil -> tree
      fiber ->
        # Run cleanup on this fiber's hook slots (see step 3b above)
        # Recursively unmount all children
        tree_without_descendants =
          Enum.reduce(fiber.children || [], tree, fn child_id, acc ->
            unmount_fiber(acc, child_id, owner_pid)
          end)
        Map.delete(tree_without_descendants, fiber_id)
    end
  end

ALSO UPDATE mount/3
The mount function in reconciler.ex has similar code. After mounting the root, use reconcile_children to correctly register all new_fibers from the initial render. Currently it does Map.merge(new_fibers) directly — this should go through reconcile_children logic to be consistent. (The root fiber has no old children on mount, so no cleanup runs, but the structure is correct.)

TESTING
  Run: mix test
  All existing tests must pass.

  Write tests in test/filament/reconciler_test.exs (create or extend):
    1. After update/4, a fiber that was present in the previous render but absent from the new render is removed from the tree AND its cleanup function is called (use a side-effect accumulator/agent to detect cleanup calls)
    2. Grandchild cleanup: if a child fiber had its own children, all are cleaned up recursively on removal
    3. Observable unsubscription: a fiber with a {:subscribed, server, value} hook slot receives an unsubscribe call when removed (use an observable stub)
    4. Children list on the parent fiber is updated to match the new render's child set
title: Item 3: Reconciler child walk using new_fibers with recursive cleanup
